content.value_statement: React 19 changes forms, async state, refs, and server boundaries. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for upgrades and new builds.
actual_capabilities: Explains React 19 Actions, Server Components, and async form patterns.
Shows useActionState, useOptimistic, use, and useTransition usage patterns.
Provides migration steps from React 18 to React 19.
Documents common breaking changes and codemod commands.
Includes security guidance for Server Actions, secrets, validation, and client boundaries.
Provides production-style examples for forms, comments, dashboards, and streaming UI.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run migrations automatically.
Examples may need adaptation for each framework, router, and data layer.
It does not replace official React or framework release notes.
Security examples require project-specific review before production use.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an Existing App
use_cases.description: Plan a React 18 to React 19 migration with breaking change checks and codemod guidance.

use_cases.title: Design Modern Form Flows
use_cases.description: Use Actions, pending states, validation, and optimistic updates for responsive form experiences.

use_cases.title: Review Server Boundaries
use_cases.description: Check where code runs, where secrets stay, and how Server Actions should validate access.

prompt_templates.title: Explain React 19 Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main React 19 changes for a developer who knows React 18. Focus on Actions, hooks, and migration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my React 18 app structure and create a React 19 migration checklist with codemods, manual fixes, and testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Action Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a React 19 form flow using useActionState, validation, pending state, and clear server/client boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Server Action Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Server Actions for authentication, authorization, input validation, secret handling, and client data exposure risks.

output_examples.input: Ask for a React 19 migration plan for an existing dashboard.
output_examples.output: A staged checklist covering dependency updates, codemods, TypeScript fixes, manual ref changes, and regression testing.

output_examples.input: Ask how to build a signup form with Actions.
output_examples.output: A design outline describing server validation, pending feedback, error handling, and where client state is needed.

output_examples.input: Ask for a Server Action security review.
output_examples.output: A concise review that flags missing authentication, unsafe secret placement, weak validation, and risky client props.

best_practices: Start migrations on React 18.3, then resolve warnings before installing React 19.
Keep secrets and privileged data inside server-only functions and Server Actions.
Validate form input and authorization before mutating data in Server Actions.
anti_patterns: Do not pass secrets or full database records into Client Components.
Do not copy migration examples without adapting them to your framework version.
Do not rely on optimistic UI without a server-side source of truth.

faq.question: Does this skill install React 19?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, and checklists. You run installation and migration commands yourself.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js 15?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include Server Components, Server Actions, and framework migration notes relevant to Next.js 15.

faq.question: Does it cover React 19 hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers useActionState, useOptimistic, use, and useTransition with usage guidance.

faq.question: Can it review security risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for authentication, authorization, validation, secret handling, and server/client boundaries.

faq.question: Is it useful for new projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides patterns for forms, streaming UI, optimistic updates, and Server Actions.

faq.question: Does it replace official React documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a practical companion and should be checked against official documentation for current releases.
